analysis.one_liner: JSW Steel is India's largest steel producer, making flat and long steel products from integrated plants in Karnataka (Vijayanagar), Odisha, and overseas units including the US.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (Oct 23, 2026) showed record crude steel output of 7.27 million tonnes and revenue of ₹54,486 crore. Reported PAT of ₹5,279 crore (attributable to owners) is up 225% YoY, but last year's base is both small and restated to exclude Bhushan Power & Steel, which was moved into a 50:50 JV with JFE in March 2026 - so this YoY comparison is not clean. Net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.28x and Moody's upgraded the company to investment-grade (Baa3) in July 2026. No confirmed date yet for Q3 FY27 results, likely late January 2027 based on past timing.
analysis.plain_terms: The headline numbers look great - record steel output, a wider profit margin, and falling debt. But the eye-catching '225% profit growth' figure is misleading: last year's comparable quarter had unusually low profit, and the company also changed what's included in last year's numbers after moving a subsidiary into a joint venture. Strip that away and the real story is steadier - more steel sold, at a slightly better margin, with the company paying down debt faster than before.
analysis.quarters: Revenue rose to ₹54,486 crore (+21% YoY, +15% QoQ). EBITDA is reported two ways - ₹10,120 crore 'operating profit' per Screener versus ₹9,941 crore 'adjusted EBITDA' elsewhere - these are not fully reconciled publicly, but on the adjusted basis the margin improved to 18.3% from 17.2% a year ago. Crude steel production hit a record 7.27 million tonnes (capacity utilisation 88%), up 10% QoQ and 5% YoY. Management flagged that prior-year figures exclude Bhushan Power & Steel (transferred to the JSW-JFE joint venture in March 2026), making YoY revenue, volume and profit comparisons not strictly comparable. Separately, a one-off ₹18,229 crore 'other income' from the Piombino Steel amalgamation hit Q4 FY26 results (not this quarter) and should be excluded from any full-year profit comparison. Management guided coking coal costs to rise a further $25/tonne in Q3 FY27, which will test whether the margin gain holds.
analysis.performance_read: The stock has strongly outperformed: +98.4% over 5 years versus Nifty's +30.4% and peer Tata Steel's +54.7%; +72.9% over 3 years versus Nifty's +21.3%. It is currently ₹1,268.9, about 5.4% below its August 26, 2026 peak of ₹1,341 - a modest pullback, not a crash. The stock underwent a 10:1 split in January 2017; the return figures supplied are already split-adjusted, so no further correction is needed there.
analysis.valuation_read: Valuation multiples are genuinely in dispute across data sources right now: P/E is quoted as low as ~10.7x and as high as ~19.7x, and EV/EBITDA ranges from roughly 7x to 15x depending on the source and whether reported or adjusted EBITDA is used. That spread is too wide to average or pick a winner from here - it needs checking against the company's own investor presentation before publishing a number. What is consistent across sources: ROE of 10.2% and ROCE of 11.0%, which for a capital-intensive steel business represent a reasonable but unremarkable mid-cycle return on capital - not evidence either way on whether the stock is cheap.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is both volume-led and margin-led, which is the more durable combination for a commodity business: crude steel production hit a record high (+10% QoQ, +5% YoY) and EBITDA margin simultaneously widened to 18.3% from 17.2%. That said, management itself flagged coking coal costs rising a further $25/tonne in Q3 FY27, so the margin half of this story has yet to be tested against rising input costs.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting into real deleveraging: net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.28x from 1.46x the prior quarter and over 3x two years ago, the company redeemed $500 million of bonds early, and Moody's, Fitch and domestic agencies have all upgraded its credit rating in 2026. Financial risk looks to be reducing. The bigger live risk is on the business/input-cost side - rising coking coal and iron ore prices, plus steel imports up 23.8% YoY (Apr-Sep 2026) despite a safeguard duty, which management wants raised further.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter (Jindal family / JSW Group) holding stands at 44.29%, down from 45.32% a year earlier - a modest reduction, not a dramatic exit. Secondary sources report 12.25% of promoter holding is pledged; this figure could not be independently confirmed against a primary exchange filing and should be checked directly before being treated as fact. FII/FPI holding has risen to 26.23% from 25.92% over the same period, with more individual FIIs on the register. No marquee global investor (sovereign fund, well-known value investor) was identified by name as newly on or absent from the register in available sources.
strengths: Record quarterly crude steel production of 7.27 million tonnes, up 10% QoQ and 5% YoY, at 88% capacity utilisation
Adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 18.3% from 17.2% a year ago even as cost pressures were building
Net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.28x from 1.46x last quarter, with early redemption of $500 million in bonds and a Moody's upgrade to investment-grade (Baa3)
5-year stock return of 98.4% comfortably ahead of Nifty's 30.4% and peer Tata Steel's 54.7%
watchpoints: Coking coal costs are guided to rise a further $25/tonne in Q3 FY27, a direct test of whether the recent margin gain holds

The widely quoted '225% YoY profit growth' is a low-base comparison further distorted by last year's figures excluding the now-JV'd Bhushan Power & Steel business - not a clean read on underlying profit trend
Promoter share pledge of 12.25% is reported only by secondary aggregators and has not been confirmed against a primary BSE/NSE filing
Finished steel imports rose 23.8% YoY (Apr-Sep 2026) despite the safeguard duty, and an anti-dumping probe into Chinese, Japanese and Russian hot-rolled steel is still unresolved
analysis.one_thing: Q3 FY27 results (expected around late January 2027, unconfirmed) showing whether the 18.3% EBITDA margin holds up against the guided $25/tonne rise in coking coal costs - that will tell whether this quarter's margin improvement was durable or temporary.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked and consistent across sources: production volumes, net debt/EBITDA, ROE (10.2%), ROCE (11.0%), and promoter holding percentage. Could not reconcile: P/E (10.7x vs 19.7x across sources), EV/EBITDA (range of 7x-15x), and two different EBITDA/PAT figures that appear to mix reported-vs-adjusted and owner-attributable-vs-consolidated bases. Promoter pledge figure (12.25%) sourced only from secondary aggregators, not a primary exchange filing - not verified, check on Screener or the BSE shareholding disclosure directly. Next results date is an estimate based on past cadence, not company-confirmed.
